summary: Preflight verification against LIVE preview backend (upload-stage-two.preview.emergentagent.com) after backend restart cleared the in-memory rate-limit window. All 8 targeted checks pass: admin login with documented password returns 200 + token; wrong password returns HTTP 401 'Invalid password' (NOT 429 — proves the slowapi limiter is not currently tripped for the requester IP); /api/auth/verify OK; and every Photo-to-Flyer preflight endpoint (themes, menu, media/assets?kind=image, photo-flyer/analyze-existing) returns 200. Dashboard SPA route reachable. Password was read from /app/memory/test_credentials.md programmatically and NEVER printed, echoed, or written to any artifact.
critical_code_review_comments: rate_limit.py uses in-memory slowapi storage — any backend restart silently clears lockouts. Consider Redis/Mongo-backed storage if the 5/15 min policy must survive restarts (security posture concern, not a functional bug).
test_credentials: Read from /app/memory/test_credentials.md — value masked (***) intentionally not propagated to this report.
seed_data_creation: None. analyze-existing test reused the first pre-existing image asset from /api/media/assets.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Documented admin password in /app/memory/test_credentials.md is VALID against the live preview backend as of iteration 30. Rate limit is 5/15min per-IP in-memory (slowapi) — a backend restart resets it. If a future test hits HTTP 429 on /api/auth/login, either wait 15 min or ask main agent to restart backend; do NOT rotate the password. Reusable pytest module at /app/backend/tests/test_auth_photoflyer_preflight.py covers login + all Photo-to-Flyer preflight endpoints.
rca of the issue: Owner saw 'Invalid password' likely because prior failed attempts had tripped the 5-attempts/15-minute per-IP rate limiter (slowapi in-memory). Backend was restarted (unrelated cause), which flushed the in-memory limiter state. Post-restart the documented password authenticates successfully and a wrong password returns 401 (not 429), confirming no active lockout. No code change required. Mitigation for the future: back the slowapi limiter with Redis or Mongo so lockouts persist across restarts, or expose an admin-only endpoint to clear the counter for a given IP.
